records.name: MCP stdio binary entry
records.purpose: The executable entry declared as the `ultimate-mcp` bin that connects the server to the stdio transport.
records.surface: See [authored signatures and interpretation](README.md). src/bin.ts is the only module that creates a StdioServerTransport. It builds the server with createMcpServer(), awaits server.connect(transport), writes a startup line to stderr and exits with code 1 on a fatal startup error. Nothing in it writes to stdout, which is the protocol wire. It is built by tsup as a separate bundle with a node shebang and is not a root export.

records.name: MCP server factory
records.purpose: Constructs the McpServer and registers the five tools with their zod input schemas, wrapping every handler so results and errors share one response shape.
records.surface: See [authored signatures and interpretation](README.md). `createMcpServer(): McpServer` creates a server named @ultimate/mcp with the hard-coded version 0.1.0 and registers search_components, get_component, get_component_api, get_component_accessibility and check_framework_compatibility. Framework arguments use the vocabulary ng, react, vue for the four component tools and angular, react, vue for check_framework_compatibility. A result object carrying a `code` field becomes an isError response with {code, message}; any thrown exception is logged to stderr and replaced by a generic internal_error. Responses are JSON text content.

records.name: Compatibility manifest reader
records.purpose: A minimal independent reader of the compatibility manifest copy shipped in the package dist, plus the module that holds its resolved path.
records.surface: See [authored signatures and interpretation](README.md). `readCompatibilityManifest(): CompatibilityManifestEntry[] | McpToolError` and `CompatibilityManifestEntry { framework: angular | react | vue; frameworkVersionRange: string }`. It reads only those two fields, returns manifest_unreadable on read, parse, non-array or malformed-entry failure, and never falls back to an empty result. `COMPATIBILITY_MANIFEST_PATH` in src/manifest-path.ts is source-only and resolves to dist/compatibility-manifest.json under the nearest package.json directory, with no fallback to docs/.

records.name: check_framework_compatibility tool
records.purpose: A single-axis check of a caller-supplied framework version against the manifest's frameworkVersionRange; not a full multi-axis compatibility verdict.
records.surface: See [authored signatures and interpretation](README.md). `checkFrameworkCompatibility(input: CheckFrameworkCompatibilityInput): CheckFrameworkCompatibilityResult | McpToolError` with input {framework: angular | react | vue; frameworkVersion: string} and result {compatible: boolean; reason?: string}. It evaluates only frameworkVersionRange with a private caret, `||` and exact range matcher that duplicates, rather than imports, the CLI matcher; unsupported grammar fails closed. It makes no claim about the Ultimate framework package, UIX, theme, schema or CLI version axes. Note the vocabulary difference: this tool takes `angular`, while the other four tools take `ng`.
